question: Should experimental Claws update planning, including the `openclaw.clawUpdatePlan.v1` consent-preview contract, be accepted as a core OpenClaw surface before the stacked apply implementation proceeds?
rationale: The patch is a new core CLI and structured contract that determines how hosts present capability escalation and consent; correctness evidence cannot decide its long-term ownership or product commitment.

options.title: Sponsor the experimental core contract
options.body: Accept this read-only planner as the core consent boundary, conditional on exact-head redaction proof and ordinary stacked-PR review.

options.title: Keep the lifecycle work but narrow the surface
options.body: Ask for a smaller internal or plugin-facing primitive before committing to the public CLI and v1 output schema.

options.title: Pause the stack
options.body: Defer the grouped Claws feature until the RFC establishes the intended core ownership and user workflow.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the experimental core contract
recommendation.body: Accept this read-only planner as the core consent boundary, conditional on exact-head redaction proof and ordinary stacked-PR review.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen is assigned to this PR and already reviewed the planner’s authoritative lifecycle and ownership boundaries.
